Status: ACTIVE (version 3)

This style guide defines how team websites in the Agentic Software Engineering lab look and behave.

--- SG-35#0 ---
[SG-35] SG-35: Page structure (ACTIVE)
# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"
3. `<footer>`, see the current footer document

The section ids are used for navigation links and MUST be exactly as given.
Additional sections (for example a "fun statistics" section) MAY be added between the two required sections.

--- SG-00#2 ---
[SG-00] SG-00: About this style guide (ACTIVE)
## Scope
The guide covers page structure, colors, theming, typography, responsive behaviour, content and tone.
It does not cover hosting, because team websites are delivered as a single local file.

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

--- SG-59#0 ---
[SG-59] SG-59: Frequently asked questions (ACTIVE)
# SG-59: Frequently asked questions

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

**Can we use Google Fonts?**
No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

**Our old site used a black night mode. Is that still ok?**
No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

**Can we use Bootstrap or Tailwind?**
Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

**What breakpoint should we use?**
The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

**One member doesn't want a photo online. What now?**
Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

**Can we add more sections?**
Yes, as long as the required sections exist, see the page structure document.

--- SG-10#0 ---
[SG-10] SG-10: Day mode palette (version 1) (DEPRECATED)
# SG-10: Day mode palette (version 1)

Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-11
Category: Color

The day mode uses a clean, neutral look.

- Page background: `#FFFFFF`
- Main text color: `#222222`
- Secondary text: `#666666`

Use these colors as CSS custom properties on the light theme. Keep the background pure white so photos look natural.

--- SG-05#1 ---
[SG-05] SG-05: Style guide changelog (ACTIVE)

- New footer text (see the current footer document). The old footer text is deprecated.
- The mobile breakpoint moved to a larger width. The old breakpoint document is deprecated.
- The storage key for the theme choice was renamed to avoid collisions with other sites.

--- SG-22#0 ---
[SG-22] SG-22: Theme toggle control (ACTIVE)
# SG-22: Theme toggle control

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

--- SG-11#0 ---
[SG-11] SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2) (ACTIVE)
# SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The day mode uses a warm, paper-like look.

- Page background MUST be `#FFF8E7` (warm off-white).
- Main text color MUST be `#1D1D1F`.
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#5A5A5F`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#FFFFFF` with a subtle shadow.

Define the colors as CSS custom properties for the light theme, for example `--bg` and `--text`,
and use the variables everywhere instead of repeating the hex values.

# SG-58: Review checklist

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

Before submitting, go through this list:

- [ ] Title and language set as described in the metadata document
- [ ] Current day and night palettes used (not the deprecated ones)
- [ ] Accent color defined as a custom property
- [ ] Theme switching and persistence implemented as described in the theming documents
- [ ] Toggle is an accessible button
- [ ] One member card per member, each with a hot take badge
- [ ] Photos have alt texts
- [ ] Required sections with the correct ids
- [ ] Exactly one h1
- [ ] Current footer text
- [ ] Current breakpoint
- [ ] System font, rem font sizes
- [ ] Reduced motion respected

[SG-21] SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2) (ACTIVE)
# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"
3. `<footer>`, see the current footer document

The section ids are used for navigation links and MUST be exactly as given.
Additional sections (for example a "fun statistics" section) MAY be added between the two required sections.

# SG-22: Theme toggle control

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.

- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

# SG-50: Responsive breakpoints (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Responsive

Team websites use exactly one layout breakpoint.

- The breakpoint MUST be written as `@media (max-width: 700px)`.
  The earlier, smaller breakpoint made cards too narrow on large phones.
- Below the breakpoint:

  - the header content is stacked vertically
  - side padding is reduced to 1rem
- The page MUST include `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`.
- Test your page at 375 px and 1280 px width. There must be no horizontal scrolling.

# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"
3. `<footer>`, see the current footer document

The section ids are used for navigation links and MUST be exactly as given.
Additional sections (for example a "fun statistics" section) MAY be added between the two required sections.

messages.content: You are building a single-file team website: task2_own_agent/site/index.html (HTML + CSS + JavaScript, nothing loaded from the internet). You cannot see the "UPB Agentic SE Web Style Guide" directly - you only know what you retrieve with search_style_guide. The guide has deprecated documents; a deprecated document names the id that replaces it. Never follow a rule from a document whose Status is DEPRECATED - look up its replacement instead. You must reply with EXACTLY ONE JSON object per turn, and nothing else outside it except, for write_site, a fenced ```html code block directly after the JSON: {"thought": "short reasoning", "action": "", "args": {...}} Actions: search_style_guide args: {"query": "..."} -> retrieved style guide chunks (<=1000 tokens) read_profiles args: {} -> team member profiles + available image files write_site args: {} (html goes in a ```html block right after the JSON, or args.html) -> saves the file and runs the full checker; returns the report finish args: {"summary": "..."} -> accepted only if the last checker report passed Rules: - Never write base64 image data yourself. Reference photos with placeholders like - the surrounding program embeds the real file. - Call read_profiles before you write the site, and search_style_guide for each area of the page you are unsure about (colors, typography, header, member cards, footer, theme toggle, etc.) before relying on a rule you have not actually retrieved. - After write_site, read the checker report. # SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Responsive

  - side padding is reduced to 1rem

- Test your page at 375 px and 1280 px width. There must be no horizontal scrolling.

# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"
3. `<footer>`, see the current footer document

The section ids are used for navigation links and MUST be exactly as given.
Additional sections (for example a "fun statistics" section) MAY be added between the two required sections.

[SG-21] SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2) (ACTIVE)
# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

- Test your page at 375 px and 1280 px width. There must be no horizontal scrolling.

# SG-55: Motion and animation

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Accessibility

Animations are allowed, but they must respect the user's settings.

- Transitions SHOULD be short (at most 300 ms). A smooth color transition when switching the theme is nice.
- If the page uses any `animation` or `transition`, it MUST include a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block
  that disables them.
- No autoplaying videos, no blinking or flashing elements.

# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

# SG-50: Responsive breakpoints (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Responsive

Team websites use exactly one layout breakpoint.

- The breakpoint MUST be written as `@media (max-width: 700px)`.

  - side padding is reduced to 1rem

- Test your page at 375 px and 1280 px width. There must be no horizontal scrolling.

# SG-52: Typography scale

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Typography

All font sizes MUST be given in `rem`. Pixel font sizes are not allowed, because they ignore the user's browser settings.

| Element | Size |
|---|---|
| body | 1rem |
| h1 | 2.5rem |
| h2 | 1.75rem |
| h3 | 1.25rem |
| hot take badge | 0.9rem |
| footer | 0.8rem |

Line height of body text: 1.6.

[SG-55] SG-55: Motion and animation (ACTIVE)
# SG-55: Motion and animation

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Accessibility

Animations are allowed, but they must respect the user's settings.

- Transitions SHOULD be short (at most 300 ms). A smooth color transition when switching the theme is nice.
- If the page uses any `animation` or `transition`, it MUST include a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block
  that disables them.
- No autoplaying videos, no blinking or flashing elements.

# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"
3. `<footer>`, see the current footer document

The section ids are used for navigation links and MUST be exactly as given.
Additional sections (for example a "fun statistics" section) MAY be added between the two required sections.

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The night mode uses a calm dark blue instead of pure black. Pure black caused eye strain in user tests.

- Page background MUST be `#14142B` (midnight blue).
- Main text color MUST be `#F4F1DE` (soft cream).
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#B8B5A7`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#1F1F3D`.

Define these colors as CSS custom properties for the dark theme. See the theme switching document for how the theme is applied.

[SG-21] SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2) (ACTIVE)
# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

# SG-50: Responsive breakpoints (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Responsive

Team websites use exactly one layout breakpoint.

- The breakpoint MUST be written as `@media (max-width: 700px)`.
  The earlier, smaller breakpoint made cards too narrow on large phones.
- Below the breakpoint:
  - member cards are shown in one column
  - the header content is stacked vertically
  - side padding is reduced to 1rem
- The page MUST include `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`.
- Test your page at 375 px and 1280 px width. There must be no horizontal scrolling.

[SG-55] SG-55: Motion and animation (ACTIVE)
# SG-55: Motion and animation

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Accessibility

Animations are allowed, but they must respect the user's settings.

- Transitions SHOULD be short (at most 300 ms). A smooth color transition when switching the theme is nice.
- If the page uses any `animation` or `transition`, it MUST include a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block
  that disables them.
- No autoplaying videos, no blinking or flashing elements.

# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:

# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

# SG-55: Motion and animation

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Accessibility

Animations are allowed, but they must respect the user's settings.

- Transitions SHOULD be short (at most 300 ms). A smooth color transition when switching the theme is nice.
- If the page uses any `animation` or `transition`, it MUST include a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block
  that disables them.
- No autoplaying videos, no blinking or flashing elements.

[SG-20] SG-20: Theme switching mechanics (ACTIVE)
# SG-20: Theme switching mechanics

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

--- SG-22#0 ---
[SG-22] SG-22: Theme toggle control (ACTIVE)
# SG-22: Theme toggle control

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

--- SG-11#0 ---
[SG-11] SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2) (ACTIVE)
# SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The day mode uses a warm, paper-like look.

- Page background MUST be `#FFF8E7` (warm off-white).
- Main text color MUST be `#1D1D1F`.
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#5A5A5F`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#FFFFFF` with a subtle shadow.

Define the colors as CSS custom properties for the light theme, for example `--bg` and `--text`,
and use the variables everywhere instead of repeating the hex values.

--- SG-14#0 ---
[SG-14] SG-14: Accent color (ACTIVE)
# SG-14: Accent color

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Color

Team websites use exactly one accent color: `#E4007C` (UPB magenta).

- The accent MUST be defined once as a CSS custom property named `--accent`, for example `:root { --accent: #E4007C; }`.
- The accent is the same in day and night mode.
- Use it only for: hot take badges, links, the focus outline and small highlights.
- Don't use the accent for large backgrounds or body text.

# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"
3. `<footer>`, see the current footer document

The section ids are used for navigation links and MUST be exactly as given.
Additional sections (for example a "fun statistics" section) MAY be added between the two required sections.

# SG-55: Motion and animation

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Accessibility

Animations are allowed, but they must respect the user's settings.

[SG-20] SG-20: Theme switching mechanics (ACTIVE)
# SG-20: Theme switching mechanics

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

[SG-22] SG-22: Theme toggle control (ACTIVE)
# SG-22: Theme toggle control

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Typography

All font sizes MUST be given in `rem`. Pixel font sizes are not allowed, because they ignore the user's browser settings.

| Element | Size |
|---|---|

| footer | 0.8rem |

  `font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;`

[SG-55] SG-55: Motion and animation (ACTIVE)
# SG-55: Motion and animation

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Accessibility

Animations are allowed, but they must respect the user's settings.

- Transitions SHOULD be short (at most 300 ms). A smooth color transition when switching the theme is nice.
- If the page uses any `animation` or `transition`, it MUST include a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block
  that disables them.
- No autoplaying videos, no blinking or flashing elements.

# SG-20: Theme switching mechanics

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

# SG-22: Theme toggle control

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

Team websites use exactly one accent color: `#E4007C` (UPB magenta).
